title: This Spacecraft Hides in a 400-Pound Titanium Vault From Jupiter

scenes.text: A spacecraft needed a metal vault to survive Jupiter.
NASA's Juno probe gets a dose like a hundred million dental X-rays.
So its electronics sit inside a titanium vault.
It weighs nearly four hundred pounds, with walls just one centimeter thick.
That cuts the radiation to one eight-hundredth.
Without the vault, Juno's brain would be fried.

description:
A spacecraft needed a metal vault to survive Jupiter.
NASA's Juno gets a radiation dose like a hundred million dental X-rays, so its electronics sit in a titanium vault weighing nearly 400 pounds.
Would you fly to Jupiter?
first_comment: Bonus: the vault cuts radiation by about 800 times, and Juno still gets damaged over time. How long can a probe last there?
